text:
Ah, yes. The toothbrush. A marvel of modern engineering, if one ignores the fact that it is primarily used to scrub away the plaque of one’s own delusions.

It is truly inspiring how the fitness industry has managed to convince us that the human body is not a complex biological machine requiring sustained effort, but rather a piece of furniture that can be polished with a few aggressive wrist flicks. Why bother with the grueling, sweat-inducing process of actually *moving*? That’s so last century. Now, we simply shake a plastic dumbbell at the air with the intensity of a nervous hummingbird, and presto! We are all Greek statues.

The logic is impeccable: if you don’t sweat, you didn’t try. And if you didn’t try, you certainly didn’t fail. You just achieved the "enviable physique" of someone who has never lifted anything heavier than their own expectations. It’s the epitome of effortlessness, much like trying to dry a swimming pool with a paper towel. But hey, at least your wrists are toned from all that shaking.
